# S20 — Meal suggestion ranking

A deterministic engine that proposes a week of dinners from the rotation (P2).

**Findings:**  · **Size:** M · **Tree:** core

**2026-11-05** — Implement deterministic dinner ranking with configurable scoring, weekly and project constraints, locked-pick alternatives, SQL loaders and documentation; verify 294 passing tests, lint, formatting and review fixes.

trust: unverified; by: Jon R

**Not in this slice:** pantry awareness (Phase 2); LLM suggestions (Later).

## Why

The point of the weekly session is starting from a good suggested plan instead of a blank week.

## Owner input

None. The planning rules interview is done (ADR 0013 Rules, S19). Owner decisions: 2026-11-04, 6 planned dinners and 1 open night per week; no repeat within 10 days; favorites rank higher; at most one project meal per week, and only on a weekend; dinners only (breakfast and lunch ingredients are staples).

Owner decisions: 2026-11-05, spec-check answers: (1) the planning week starts on Sunday and covers the 7 nights after the Saturday-evening session; the weekend is Saturday and Sunday, so a project meal may fall only on those days; (2) suggest_week returns ranked picks for all 7 nights and the planning session (S21) drops whichever night the household marks open; (3) rank.py is pure functions on plain data (candidate, history, rules and seed dataclasses) and never touches SQLite; two loader functions (rotation candidates, made-or-planned history) go in src/larder/planner_db.py, which joins this slice's files with src/larder/planner/__init__.py, and alternatives takes the in-progress week with its locked picks plus the night; (4) any in-rotation recipe whose meal_type is null or 'dinner' is a candidate.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-05, spec-check answer: when the eligible pool is smaller than the nights to fill, relax the 10-day repeat gap: reuse the least-recently-made meals past the gap, but never repeat a meal within the week, so a pool smaller than 7 still leaves some nights empty for the household to fill in the planning session.

## Implement

1. Score = recency + favorite weight + effort fit, as pure functions with the rules from ADR 0013.
2. Produce N picks for the configured nights, avoiding repeats within the week.
3. Expose `suggest_week(date, rules, history)` and `alternatives(slot, k)` for swapping.
4. Seeded randomness for tie-breaks so the output is reproducible.
